title: Peptide Vial Labels in Trays: Test Scuffing Before You Order the Roll
seoTitle: Peptide Vial Label Tray Scuff Test | RP Labels
description: A custom vial label can look perfect on the bench and rub in a transport tray. Plan an applied-vial scuff and edge-lift proof before bulk printing.
alt: AI-generated RP Research branded peptide sample vials in a molded tray with a printed label proof and inspection magnifier
caption: AI-generated packaging scenario. RP Research artwork, DEMO 042 lot and codes are fictional; tray abrasion performance was not tested by this image.
intro: A vial label that survives hand application may still scuff where its face or edge touches the transport tray.
related: Check edge lift on small vials
sources: Avery Dennison: overlaminates and abrasion protection

title: Peptide Vial Labels for Camera Inspection: Approve the Applied View
seoTitle: Peptide Vial Label Camera Inspection Proof | RP
description: Plan a custom peptide vial label for the real camera angle, label seam and variable-code field, then prove it on the actual inspection station.
alt: AI-generated RP Research peptide sample vial with branded wrap label under a camera inspection head on a labeling line
caption: AI-generated machine-vision scene. The pictured RP Research code is illustrative and has not been verified by a production camera.
intro: An artwork proof can pass while the installed camera only sees a seam, a glare band or half of the variable code.
sources: HERMA: 211 HC wrap-around labeler camera and print verification

title: Supplement Stick Packs and Cartons: Decide Which Copy Lives Where
seoTitle: Supplement Stick Pack and Carton Label Guide | RP
description: Before printing single-serve supplement sticks and an outer carton, map the sale unit, principal display panel and Supplement Facts responsibilities.
alt: AI-generated RP Wellness branded single-serve stick packs and matching outer carton showing distinct front and information panels
caption: AI-generated concept. The pictured ingredients, Facts numbers, serving claims and DEMO artwork are fictional and not an approved or verified formula.
intro: A box of single-serve sticks is really two artwork jobs, and the answer changes when a stick may be sold on its own.
sources: FDA: dietary supplement small and multiunit package provisions

title: Supplement Labels: Leave a Real Place for Net Contents on the Front
seoTitle: Supplement Label Net Contents Front Panel Proof | RP
description: Reserve the net quantity statement on the real principal display panel before decoration, trim and a bottle curve consume the usable area.
alt: AI-generated RP Wellness supplement bottles with branded front labels and separate printed Supplement Facts artwork proof
caption: AI-generated layout example only. Formula, Facts figures, net quantities and claims in the illustration are fictional and require product-specific regulatory review.
intro: The lower part of a supplement front label is often treated as decoration space until the net-quantity line arrives.
sources: FDA: net quantity of contents on dietary supplements
FDA: general dietary supplement labeling and display panels

title: Hologram Plus QR Labels: Give Visual and Digital Checks Separate Jobs
seoTitle: Hologram Visual Check vs QR Verification | RP
description: Specify what a buyer should inspect on a custom hologram and what a QR destination should verify, without assuming either feature alone stops copying.
alt: AI-generated RP Secure holographic visual cue and separate QR demonstration patch on two branded cartons beside a phone
caption: AI-generated security-label concept. The illustrated QR is not a working verification service; the RP Secure mark and carton brand are fictional.
intro: A reflective mark catches the eye, while a QR code starts a digital check. They should not be sold as the same security feature.
sources: GS1: digital signatures and physical security markings
GS1: 2D barcode quiet zones and print conditions
